content.thinking:
I'm planning the scale and layout of the scene—a workbench roughly 1.6m wide with a shelf riser and a stool—and thinking through how to structure the objects, noting that the builder needs exactly one root joint while most props can remain plain objects.

I'm setting up helper functions for boxes, cylinders, spheres, and lathe shapes (like bottles), all anchored to a single root joint, while keeping the color palette efficient by reusing paint constants for wood grain and brass materials to stay under the distinct-color budget.

For the bottles, I'm designing a lathe outline that shapes a flask-like silhouette with a glass body and pale neck, adding glow to the liquid for a magical effect, and making sure the profile points avoid self-intersection with enough segments for smoothness. Now I'm positioning the table surface and starting on its dimensions.

Now I'm defining the tabletop slab with overhang trim and wood grain paint textures, plus darker trim and brass accents, and adding a cloth runner with striped detailing on top of the table.

For the runner, I'll use alpha-cut textures so the pendant ends in a point with a diamond shape. For the green cloth drape on the left, I'm positioning a thin vertical plane near the table's left edge, being careful it doesn't clip into the table legs positioned at ±0.8.

Now I'm laying out the legs, feet, gold corner caps, and lower shelf with specific box dimensions and positions, plus starting the front apron box.

Adding drawer cabinet and brass pulls...

Now I'm adding the back riser posts for a hanging bar setup, with brass cross rod and finial spheres, plus hanging herb bundles for detail.

Still writing bundle textures...

Then I'm placing a back shelf on the riser around y=1.15, matching the reference's bottle display area.

Beyond that, I need a backsplash board, a book stack, and a scale centered on the shelf. I'm mapping out the x-axis layout left to right: crystal bowl and candle on the far left, mortar and pestle next, then herb rack posts further along.

Continuing right, I'll place the scale centered on the table, a stack of five books nearby, then the distillation apparatus cluster with its brass stand, flask, burner, coil tube, and test tube rack. I need to resolve a spacing conflict between the amethyst bowl and herb rack by shifting the rack slightly left, add spoons on the runner, and put a stool at the front right corner.

Now I'm detailing the stool itself with a cushioned seat, tapering legs, rungs, and brass caps, then filling in under-shelf items like the green bottle, herb crate, and sack, placing a hanging leather pouch with scrolls on the left side over the cloth, and considering a small ornate brass lantern ornament hanging there too.

I'm finishing the hanging ornament with a chain, sphere, dark inner ring, and teal crystal pendant below it, while confirming part count stays well under the limit and checking overall height dimensions fit within the apparatus scale. Now I'm starting to write the actual construction code, setting up helper function signatures and types for geometry and bone attachments.

Writing helper functions...

Defining wood grain paints...

I'm checking the pendant's z-position against the drawer fronts and table top overhang to make sure it clears the cabinet geometry without clipping through other elements.

Now I'm sketching the pendant and runner artwork: a diamond-pointed cream pendant shape with green borders, a gold diamond accent, and tassel details, plus a cream table runner featuring green side stripes and a repeated gold diamond pattern. Next I'm thinking through what small objects to place on the runner, like spoons with their scoop and handle shapes.

For the stacked books, I'm structuring each as a colored cover box slightly larger than a cream pages block, offsetting the pages block in depth so the spine edge of the cover remains visible on the front-facing side, stacking five of them slightly askew for a casual look.

Now I'm designing the scale: a lathed brass base, a column rod, a slightly rotated beam box, and pans hanging from chains made of thin rods connecting to shallow dome-shaped lathed bowls, making sure the pan outline points don't self-intersect.

Positioning the scale on the table with the column rising to the beam, pans hanging below with crystal in one and herb in the other, I need to nudge the scale's x-position so its beam doesn't collide with the herb rack posts nearby. Then I'm placing the herb rack with a crossbar and hanging bundles at varying x-positions, with a shelf below them.

I'm working out the shelf and bottle placement so bottle tops clear the hanging bundles above, spacing bottles evenly along the shelf, and checking whether a backsplash board behind the posts needs its own z-offset to avoid overlapping the post width.

Now I'm building the distillation apparatus: a brass lamp base with a glowing flame, a four-legged brass stand rising to a ring plate, and preparing to place a round flask on top of it.

Still shaping liquid geometry...

Still working out the pipe curve from the flask neck down into the coil, adjusting coordinates so it connects cleanly at the brass stopper collar before descending to the receiver flask.

I'm also adding a decorative brass stand element to the left of the apparatus, with a vertical post curving into an arc near the top, positioned to hang over the flask area—keeping it simple with just a holder ring rather than a full ornament.

Settling the bulb-and-chain geometry with a quadratic bezier path, then moving to design a small test tube rack: a brass/wood base with uprights holding five glowing glass tubes of colored liquid, sized and positioned near the flask.

I'm also adding decorative elements—a brass bowl with amethyst cone crystals on the right, a matching crystal cluster bowl on the left with six-sided tilted cones glowing blue-purple, and starting on a candle dish nearby.

Now I'm shaping the mortar and pestle: a white marble lathe profile for the hollow mortar, a tilted cylinder with a ball tip for the pestle, and small green card/ellipsoid shapes for herbs sitting inside and scattered loosely on the table.

Scattering around 14 small leaf-card sprigs with a randomized circular flow pattern near x -0.7 to -0.3 and x 0.2, lying flat at y 0.903, then moving on to the lower shelf where I'll place a tall green lathe-profile bottle near x -0.1.

Adding a dark wood crate with leafy cards stacked on top, a tied sack bundle, and small colored bottles (blue and amber) nearby, working out their x/z positions to avoid overlapping the cabinet and crate footprints.

Now I'm placing a stool in front of the drawers with splayed legs, a rung connecting them, a wooden seat frame topped with a green cushion and patterned surface, plus brass corner caps. Nearby I'm adding a leather pouch with an angled flap and brass buckle, positioning it slightly behind the stool.

I'm also working out a hanging lantern ornament near the left front leg, chaining down from the tabletop area through a brass sphere with dark ring details to a crystal pendant below, making sure to adjust its position so it doesn't collide with the nearby cloth.

For the teal cloth itself, I'm defining its extent on the table—centering it along part of the table's left side with gold trim at the edges—and making sure the crystals and mortar items placed on top sit at a consistent height just above the cloth surface, simplifying its coverage to just part of the tabletop rather than the whole span.

Then for the hanging drape on the left side, I'm planning a dark teal plane with gold border and pointed tail descending from the table edge, spanning roughly 0.65 units in height, oriented facing outward with its width running along the z-axis.

I'm also adding decorative hardware: brass corner plates at the leg tops, an edge trim strip along the front of the tabletop, and brass diamond-shaped plates rotated 45 degrees for the carved diamond motif.

Now I'm positioning diagonal corner braces between the legs and aprons for structural detail, plus defining the top slab dimensions with an underlying apron frame box, then working out where the front apron panel sits relative to the cabinet section.

Continuing to figure out apron placements around the sides and back, then I'm sizing and positioning the cabinet box itself along with its drawer fronts, aligning their depths so the drawer faces sit flush against the cabinet front.

I'm adding hardware details — a brass diamond plate and ring pull centered on each drawer front, plus matching legs positioned under the cabinet, and a lower shelf board spanning between the legs.

Now I'm working out feet details for the legs, orienting a cushion plane facing upward, and setting up the herb texture SVGs — lavender with purple ellipse clusters and leaf shapes built from looped stem-and-ellipse patterns, keeping a shared color palette for consistency.

For the hanging bundles, I'm figuring out a ring of frames around each stem position so they fan outward, adjusting the lean angle to control whether the bundles point straight down or angle outward from the center.

Now I'm designing the potion bottles for the shelf—each built from a single lathe shape colored by liquid with a touch of glow to make them read bright against a duller glass tint, plus a pale glass neck and cork for that cel-shaded flask look.

Defining potion shape variants...

I'm positioning the label slightly embedded on the bottle face and figuring out the stopper design—a cork cylinder with a small brass ball on top for the ornate variants. Now I'm starting to write the actual TypeScript code, setting up a local Fill type to avoid import issues before building the helper functions.

Writing helper functions...

Still sketching outline coordinates...

Now I'm setting up the scene file with imports for the builder, frame, path utilities, and paint/texture helpers before writing the actual object construction code.

Defining the color palette...

I'm bumping paintSize to 2048 for crisper texture detail given the total painted area across the piece, and now sketching out the leg geometry loop with positions mirrored on both axes.

Adding foot pads, brass caps, and corner gussets...

Still adding brass bands and diamond accents...

Now I'm figuring out bottle placement on the shelf, then starting a potion-bottle generator function that builds different outline shapes per variant based on radius, parameterizing the round-bottle silhouette with a series of width/height points.

I'm fixing a self-overlapping segment in the outline where the path doubled back on itself, simplifying it to a clean final point, with the lip handled separately as a glass ring cylinder, topped by a cork and brass cap. Now I'm starting the conical variant's outline points...

Finishing the conical bottle outline and sketching a square apothecary alternative using a 4-segment lathe shape, then noting the top heights for each variant and planning to add a flat-colored glow effect plus a thin cream label plane.

I'll skip labels on variants 1 and 2, only applying one to variant 0, and confirm the glow function works directly on flat color strings. Then I'm designing a crystal builder function that creates a cone tip with a hexagonal cylinder shaft, parameterized by position, height, radius, color, tilt, and rotation.

Building the lathe outline for the crystal shaft and tip...

I'll cluster six crystals together with varying tilts, then move on to shaping the candle flame as a scaled ball.

Now I'm working out the scales: a brass base lathe with tapered profile, a thin column rod extending upward, a finial ball with a diamond accent on top, and a connecting beam rod set at a slight tilt.

Writing scale pans and chains...

Now I'm checking for collisions between the book stack and the apparatus stand, since the scale footprint overlaps with the flask and rack positions. I need to shift the books' x-position to keep clear spacing from the stand rod.

Adjusting apparatus placement — moving the arm, flask, coil, and receiver rightward while making sure the receiver tube stays within the table's right edge limit.

Now I'm positioning the test tube rack and bowl, then checking the books' footprint against the spoon runner to confirm the books sit properly on top of the runner without overlapping other items.

I'm standardizing a base y-value of 0.906 for items sitting on surfaces, checking the runner's footprint against the scale base and cloth placement, and verifying the runner's overall span relative to the pendant and other nearby objects to catch any overlap issues.

Now I'm adding smaller tabletop props—a lying parchment scroll with brass-wood end caps near the cloth, plus a small inkpot and quill—placing each at specific coordinates on the table surface.

I'm working out the final assembly, including a herb-bundle helper function that generates card frames in a ring pattern to simulate hanging foliage, using the cards API with size, lean, and flow parameters.

Each bundle (lavender, leaf, white) gets its own texture, and I'm adding a tie element and small cylinder/ball details to represent twine wrapping around the bundle base.

Writing SVG texture code...

Adding the tassel rod with a brass ball and cream cone shape, then moving to the hanging cloth SVG—a teal pennant with a pointed bottom edge, gold border lines, and an embroidered diamond pattern, sized to match the plane dimensions.

Now I'm starting the full component build, aiming for roughly 450 lines while keeping TypeScript strict mode happy by avoiding unused locals and wrapping box helpers in glow effects. Writing the module metadata and type definitions...

Still writing helper functions...

For the hanging lantern, I'm thinking a cage design instead of solid ball: a glowing orange core sphere surrounded by three brass-dark torus rings rotated along different axes to form a lattice. I'll top it with a cone cap and add a pendant crystal spike below using a downward-pointing lathe axis for a teal glow effect.

Now I'm working out the apparatus stand geometry — vertical corner rods, a horizontal mounting plate, and positioning the flask so it sits properly on the ring, with a burner lamp lathe shape and flame placed beneath it, making sure the spacing between the lamp and plate works out correctly.

Now I'm defining a flaskBall helper that builds a glass sphere, a glowing liquid hemisphere inside it, and a rotated disc to cap the liquid surface so it faces upward.

Still plotting pipe geometry...

Checking the cork geometry so the pipe end sits just inside the cork top—looks good with the numbers lining up. Now I'm positioning the coil sweep and support arm, using a bezier curve for the arm geometry with glass material.

Adding bulb and rod geometry...

Still placing glassware details...

Now I'm positioning the crystal bowls on each side -- a brass pedestal with amethyst crystals on the right, and a taller pedestal with larger blue-violet crystals on the left.

I'm also adding a candle dish setup with dripping wax detail, and working out the mortar and pestle placement -- tilting the pestle at an angle so it leans out of the bowl with its rounded top end positioned correctly relative to the rotation.

For the marble texture, I'm using a mottled paint pattern mixing cream and grey tones to simulate stone veining. Then I'm scattering loose herb sprites around the cloth and table runner using a flow function for natural variation, plus adding an ink pot, a small pouch with a flap, and deciding to skip the quill for now.

Positioning the pouch details now — buckle, strap running up to the tabletop edge, and three rolled scrolls with small rings at the top standing near the pouch. I'm also placing a hanging lantern near the table leg and working out where its chain attaches above.

Adding more geometry...

Adding more stool details...

Now I'm placing the potion bottles on the shelf, checking that their positions don't collide with the support posts -- making sure the bottle radius and post width leave enough clearance at each x-coordinate.

Checking the smaller bottle at x -0.86 and the height clearances for the bundle heights against the cork tops — looks fine. I'll add a few more potions near the lower shelf and books, then write out the final file.
